parties.petitioner_plaintiff: Petitioner (wife) — filed petition for restitution of conjugal rights
parties.respondent_defendant: Respondent-husband — filed appeal against trial court order

facts_of_case: Petitioner (wife) claimed restitution of conjugal rights after respondent-husband failed to take care of her and their child; respondent denied relationship and marriage; trial court allowed petition; respondent appealed to District Court, Tirunelveli

legal_principles.principle: A Hindu marriage can be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto.
legal_principles.held: As per Section 7 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955, a Hindu marriage can be solemnized in accordance with the customary rites and ceremonies of either party thereto

legal_principles.principle: A marriage by mere tying of the thali is a valid marriage.
legal_principles.held: Sec.7A (1) (c) include marriage by mere tying of the thali
cited_cases: Mathialaqan. K. v. Mala Devi, 1989 (2) L.W. 361

legal_principles.principle: The evidence of P.Ws.1 and 2 are more probable and acceptable.
legal_principles.held: The evidence of P.Ws.l and 2 are more probable and acceptable

outcome.final_order: Trial court order set aside by lower appellate court, but wife's appeal against that order was allowed

keywords: Latin maxim: Nemo dat quod non habet
use_for_drafting: drafting divorce petition under Hindu Marriage Act
advising on restitution of conjugal rights
appealing family court order to District Court
